status: Local source/API feasibility review; no CUDA execution, new kernels, models or capture analysis
answer: Practical exact-real-arithmetic mass preservation needs full-row normalization or an equivalent auxiliary mass channel. Current public SDPA output and existing telemetry do not expose it. Installed cuDNN/Flash ATen operators already return LSE, so replacing the one full attention call can obtain it without a second image-attention pass or a newly written custom kernel. CUDA support, baseline parity and throughput remain untested.

local_interfaces.public_sdpa: torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention returns only output Tensor; no LSE or attention-mass argument.

aten_schemas._scaled_dot_product_flash_attention: aten::_scaled_dot_product_flash_attention(Tensor query, Tensor key, Tensor value, float dropout_p=0., bool is_causal=False, bool return_debug_mask=False, *, float? scale=None) -> (Tensor output, Tensor logsumexp, Tensor cum_seq_q, Tensor cum_seq_k, SymInt max_q, SymInt max_k, Tensor rng_state, Tensor unused, Tensor debug_attn_mask)

local_interfaces.cudnn: Pass attn_bias=None, compute_log_sumexp=True, dropout_p=0, is_causal=False, return_debug_mask=False, scale=1/sqrt128. Meta specifies output B,H,S,D and FP32 LSE B,H,S,1.
local_interfaces.flash: ATen _scaled_dot_product_flash_attention returns output and FP32 LSE B,H,S even without debug mask. It is a different explicit backend from current cuDNN-first priority.
local_interfaces.efficient: ATen efficient attention also has compute_log_sumexp=True; metadata can pad row length to a multiple of32.
local_interfaces.public_varlen: torch.nn.attention.varlen.varlen_attn exposes return_aux=AuxRequest(lse=True), but installed _should_use_cudnn returns False. This wrapper takes T,H,D packed sequences and invokes Flash. Its doc/fake metadata differ in LSE axis wording, so verify actual layout rather than assume it.
local_interfaces.public_flex: flex_attention return_aux=AuxRequest(lse=True) exposes LSE with explicit internal base2-to-natural-log conversion. This changes kernel/compile path and is not a drop-in preservation of current cuDNN attention.
local_interfaces.existing_telemetry: CR19 payloads contain selected Q/K/V/output/gains, not kernel LSE. Offline rows provide only the sampled192 full normalization values. Backend priority is not proof of which backend executed; no whole-model mass stream is cached.

operator.fixed_mass: y_new=y_old+m*(u_new_text-u_old_text). Equivalent in real arithmetic to shifting all new text logits by LSE_old_text-LSE_new_text, leaving image logits and total text probability unchanged.
operator.target_phase: Native endpoint map p*63/(L-1), base theta10000, axis0 unchanged; all512 text keys including padding. Preserve pre-RoPE normalized image Q for alternate rotation, then apply the same BF16 pair gains. Inverting already-rounded captured Q is only a surrogate.
operator.scope: Text-query rows copied from baseline within each attention call. This does not imply all later-layer text states remain unchanged after image states are modified.
operator.mass_not_identifiable_from_output_alone: General128-dimensional attention output does not identify the total probability on a512-key subset among66048keys. Recomputing text LSE alone does not supply the full normalizer.

viable_route: One explicit cuDNN output+LSE baseline over the full joint sequence, with the existing post-RoPE BF16 gain multiplication and layout. Keep all original outputs, including text-query rows.
Compute old and phase-altered image-query-to-text-only attention pools with the same gains/scale, obtaining old text LSE; new text LSE is needed for the unnormalized comparison arm.

Use FP32 LSE differences and merge arithmetic, cast resulting image rows back to the original dtype. Text branches can be query-chunked while all512text keys remain present. No dense N-by-N score tensor.
Require an unsupported-kernel error rather than a large math fallback. First future GPU use needs baseline/repeat/no-op and tiny dense-oracle comparisons; no GPU validation is claimed here.
cost_scope: Multiply+add=2FLOPs; both QK and PV counted. Excludes softmax/reductions, projection layers, phase rotation, merge, launch/layout costs, kernel workspaces, full-model wall time and all claims of speed. Multiplying by57 or28 assumes intervention on all calls/steps; tensors need not persist across calls.
memory_interpretation: At4K, straightforward alternate Q plus two BF16 conditional outputs and LSE buffers cost1.227GB beyond baseline tensors. An FP32 merge buffer adds805MB; kernel/phase temporaries are additional.

With4096-query chunks, alternateQ and two outputs total75.50MB; full baseline LSE6.34MB, two chunk LSEs0.786MB, mass0.393MB, and one FP32 merge buffer50.33MB totalabout133.35MB. Retaining pre-RoPE Q for faithful alternate rotation addsabout405.8MB if kept for the entire joint sequence, or precompute full alternateQ and stream the pool branches.
Existing text K/V can be views; optional contiguous copies add6.29MB. Unfused text logits alone cost3.22GB per matrix at4K, so fused or chunked computation is preferable.

At1024 native resolution there are4096image tokens, not65536; the same two-branch overhead is19.75percent of dense attention arithmetic. Identity phase should bypass interventions when scientifically allowed, but no such shortcut has been implemented.
numerical_obstacles: Real-arithmetic partition preservation does not guarantee BF16 byte equivalence. Separate softmax kernels and output subtraction have rounding error; establish no-op residual explicitly.
LSE shapes/base convention and compute_log_sumexp inference behavior must be checked on the actual CUDA operator; local schemas are not execution proof.

Unnormalized phase uses log-domain partition reweighting. If original text mass rounds to1 and strong downweighting exposes an image contribution lost in BF16 output, stable exact recovery from baseline-minus-text is not guaranteed without separately evaluating image conditional attention.

Switching from automatic public SDPA to explicit cuDNN removes automatic backend fallback; unsupported shapes/layouts should fail explicitly. Returning LSE can change backend graph/kernel choice even for identical mathematical attention.
alternative_mass_channel: Appending a text-indicator coordinate to V could return m with the baseline output in real arithmetic, avoiding LSE. It changes value head width and backend constraints; support, padding, numerical precision and cost are unverified. This is not a cleaner established route than the installed LSE-returning kernels.
